failed_items.claim: scripts/telemetry-master-off.py's docstring claim that the two inline python3 -c copies are 'equivalent in what they decide, differing only in the env var each passes the config path through' is true against HEAD
failed_items.evidence: False. scripts/config-get.sh's inline copy is `except Exception: sys.exit(1)` with `tel = data.get("telemetry") if isinstance(data, dict) else None` — a two-way {0,1} contract with no exit-2 branch. scripts/telemetry-master-off.py and lib/efficiency-trace.sh's inline copy both carry the three-way {0,1,2} contract (FileNotFoundError -> 1, other Exception -> 2, non-dict -> 2). Empirically verified: `python3 scripts/telemetry-master-off.py <corrupt>` exits 2, `<missing>` exits 1. The copies therefore differ in what they decide at exit-code granularity, and in more than the env var. The same docstring instructs 'Change the decision here, change it in all three', which iteration 3 itself did not do when it introduced exit 2.

failed_items.claim: scripts/collect-staged-telemetry.sh's two diff-added gate comments state consequences that are true against HEAD
failed_items.evidence: Both are false. (a) Line 34: 'an empty anchor would silently no-op this gate' — an empty _CST_DIR makes `[ ! -f "$_CST_DIR/telemetry-master-off.py" ]` test /telemetry-master-off.py, miss, and emit the loud `::warning::collect-staged-telemetry: telemetry-master-off.py not found beside this script — the telemetry.enabled master switch was NOT consulted` arm; the script runs under `set -uo pipefail` with no -e so it does not abort. Verified by invoking the script by a slash-free argv[0] through PATH: rc 0 with the warning emitted, not a silent no-op. (b) Lines 43-44: spelling .prflow/ 'would make this gate miss a mid-migration .devflow/ consumer's master switch and upload the payload their sibling --persist gate skipped' — the collection loop globs only "$ROOT"/.prflow/tmp/telemetry-stage-*/ (line 75) and the producer stages only under "${root}"/.prflow/tmp/telemetry-stage-* (lib/efficiency-trace.sh:1787,1806); neither honors the .devflow/ read-through, so a .devflow/-only consumer has no payload at that path to upload. The config read-through itself is correct; only the stated consequences are false.

failed_items.claim: The shipped external doc's cost figure 'measured at roughly 1-3% of a run' has a recorded provenance in the repository, or is registered as an exempt checked-in literal under CLAUDE.md's issue-#656 convention
failed_items.evidence: Neither. `grep -rn '1–3%'` over docs/internal/ and .prflow/logs/ returns nothing; the figure traces only to issue #2035's own unsourced User Impact section (.prflow/tmp/issue-body/issue-2035.md:13). It is a precise-sounding measured figure in shipped, published customer docs presented as current fact, with nothing generating or pinning it.
